# Spark plug and intake plenum gasket replacement

> **[Unverified]** This page rests on a single community report. Cross-check before relying on it.

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

[Partial] Remove ignition coils and intake plenum, then install new or swapped spark plugs. [t327]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. Remove the ignition coil on Cylinder #1 to access the spark plug.
2. Extract the spark plug and inspect its condition.
3. If necessary, remove the intake plenum for better clearance around all cylinders.
4. [Partial] Install new or swapped spark plugs into their respective locations (2-4-6 top row, 3-5 bottom row).
5. Reinstall ignition coils onto the spark plug boots.

_Procedure reported by [t327]._

## Tips & gotchas

- [Partial] Use dielectric grease on connectors to prevent swelling gaskets from interfering with connection. [t327]
- [Partial] Swap plugs between banks if unsure which one is misfiring before buying new ones. [t327]

## Common mistakes

- Struggling to align the coil connector due to a swollen spark plug boot gasket. [t327]
- [Partial] Tearing off an old rubber gasket while trying to clean it out instead of replacing it. [t327]
